solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Some champagne and fresh soup, a great production (6,4)

indicators.note: a fresh version of something is a new arrangement of it

blocks.note: a magnum is a large bottle, here of champagne

annotation.surface: A lavish dinner party with bubbly and a new soup, staged like a grand show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Some champagne' reads as a quantity, but a magnum is a specific bottle size, twice the standard.
annotation.definitionFit: A magnum opus is a great work, an artist's masterpiece.

entries.clue: Impenetrable expression on drunk (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on top of another comes first

blocks.note: an air is an expression or look (an air of boredom)

annotation.surface: Someone's face goes blank and unreadable after a few drinks.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'impenetrable' with 'expression' to suggest a poker face; 'expression' is really the look sense of AIR.
annotation.definitionFit: Airtight means sealed so nothing can get through: impenetrable.

entries.clue: Indicate agreement with what makes herds hers? (3)

blocks.note: turning one word into the other needs a lack, a 'no'
the letter HERDS has and HERS does not

annotation.surface: A farmer's playful question about how cattle become hers.
annotation.walkthrough: The question reads like ownership of livestock, but it is about spelling: HERDS becomes HERS with no D.
annotation.definitionFit: To nod is to show agreement with a dip of the head.

entries.clue: This study suggests something to chew on (3,2)

indicators.note: the answer, read as its own clue, points to something else

blocks.note: chewing gum, the thing you chew; it is the answer's first word read upwards

annotation.surface: A study that gives you food for thought.
annotation.walkthrough: Read MUG UP as though it were a clue in a down entry: MUG going up gives GUM, something to chew. 'Chew on' pretends to mean 'think about'.
annotation.definitionFit: To mug up is British slang for studying hard, cramming.

entries.clue: Feeble child’s loose coat (7)

blocks.note: a tot is a small child; the 's joins it on

annotation.surface: A sickly child dressed in a baggy coat.
annotation.walkthrough: PALETOT is a less familiar word, so the wordplay does the work: both pieces are standard.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the paletot is a named style of loose outer garment, borrowed from French.

entries.clue: Leader of assault was fast catching a big bird (9)

indicators.note: one piece catches another by holding it inside

blocks.note: A + RHEA, a large flightless South American bird

annotation.surface: A fast attacker grabbing an ostrich-like bird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Was fast' suggests fasting or holding firm, but here it is simply speed.
annotation.definitionFit: The spearhead is the leading force of an attack.

entries.clue: Willing to risk being dismissed by phone (4)

indicators.note: on the phone you only hear a word, so its spelling can change

blocks.note: in cricket, a batsman bowled is out, dismissed

annotation.surface: Someone takes a chance on being fired over the phone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dismissed' sounds like losing a job; in cricket a batsman is out when bowled, the ball hitting the stumps.
annotation.definitionFit: Bold means daring, willing to take risks.

entries.clue: Sacked minister perhaps put money on senior lawyer (11)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

blocks.note: to back a horse is to bet on it
a bencher is a senior member of one of London's Inns of Court

annotation.surface: A sacked politician gambling on the outcome of a top lawyer's case.
annotation.walkthrough: In British politics a backbencher is an MP without a government post, so a sacked minister goes back to the back benches. 'Perhaps' flags the definition as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A minister who loses office usually returns to the back benches of Parliament.

entries.clue: Boy looking embarrassed to go up climbing frame (6)

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading bottom to top

annotation.surface: A blushing boy scrambling up the playground climbing frame.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Climbing frame' suggests playground equipment; a ladder is simply a frame for climbing.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: literally a frame you climb, though the phrase usually means playground kit.

entries.clue: Wasteful for convict to lie about biting detective (8)

indicators.note: turned about means reversed
the outer letters bite into, and so hold, the inner piece

blocks.note: an old lag is a convict
surface padding: it makes the convict lie and gives no letters

annotation.surface: A convict is lying about having bitten a police detective.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole of the first two pieces does the biting, not just the convict. 'Old lag' is British slang for a habitual prisoner.
annotation.definitionFit: Prodigal means recklessly wasteful, as in the prodigal son.

entries.clue: Render unreadable poem on fence, ripping the edges (6)

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it
tearing off a word's first and last letters

annotation.surface: A vandal tearing a poem posted on a fence so no one can read it.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures someone destroying a notice; unreadable here means scrambled into code.
annotation.definitionFit: To encode is to put into code, making a message unreadable to outsiders.

entries.clue: Withdraw medicine providing stimulant (6)

indicators.note: drawing something back reverses it

blocks.note: a pill is a dose of medicine

annotation.surface: A doctor stopping a prescription that contained a stimulant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Withdraw' sounds like stopping medication; it reverses PILL IF.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small boost that livens things up, as in a fillip to sales.

entries.clue: Remained shocked after stage trickery (11)

indicators.note: shocked letters are jolted out of order
the anagram comes after the other piece

blocks.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race

annotation.surface: Someone stayed stunned after a magician's stage act.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stage trickery' reads as a theatre illusion, but 'stage' is a leg of a journey and the definition is 'trickery' alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Legerdemain is sleight of hand, hence trickery.

entries.clue: Half of them held up beat (8)

indicators.note: take half the letters of the word that follows

annotation.surface: Half of a group were mugged and beaten.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests 'beat' as assault; it is the past tense of beat as a pulse does.
annotation.definitionFit: Throbbed means beat rhythmically, like a heart.

entries.clue: I predict our team will be absorbed by next book (3,2-7)

indicators.note: what is absorbed ends up inside the other piece

blocks.note: the ego is the self, the 'I'

annotation.surface: A fan forecasting that their team will be taken over by the next big thing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I predict' reads as one phrase, but each word is its own piece. The book is L. P. Hartley's 1953 novel, famous for its opening 'The past is a foreign country'.
annotation.definitionFit: The Go-Between is a well-known English novel by L. P. Hartley.

entries.clue: Confidence about a senior sculptor’s work (3,6)

indicators.note: one piece goes about, around, the other

blocks.note: A + SR, the abbreviation for senior

annotation.surface: An older sculptor's self-assurance about their work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Senior' abbreviates to SR, as in names like John Smith Sr.
annotation.definitionFit: Bas-relief is low-relief sculpture, carved so figures barely stand out from the background.

entries.clue: Criminal skinned fish to overstep boundaries (8)

indicators.note: a skinned word has its outer letters removed

blocks.note: a fence is a criminal who deals in stolen goods; FENCE skinned leaves ENC
the roach is a freshwater fish

annotation.surface: A crook gutting a fish while trespassing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Skinned' makes the surface sound like gutting a fish, but it applies to the criminal; a fence receives stolen goods. The same ENC turned up in 10 across.
annotation.definitionFit: To encroach is to intrude beyond proper limits.

entries.clue: Early morning call having gone off, she ran inside (4,3,5)

indicators.note: something that has gone off has gone wrong, its letters spoiled

annotation.surface: An alarm clock went off and she dashed back into the house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Having gone off' fits the alarm clock picture perfectly, which hides it as the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: "Rise and shine!" is the cheerful call used to wake someone.

entries.clue: Professional in practice getting Romeo to replace two lines (7)

indicators.note: one piece goes in where another comes out

blocks.note: Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: An actor in rehearsal getting Romeo to swap a couple of lines.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a theatre rehearsal; 'in practice' is really 'actually'. ACTUALLY with R replacing LL gives ACTUARY.
annotation.definitionFit: An actuary is a professional who calculates insurance risks.

entries.clue: I’m surprised I can wear extra short fabric (6)

indicators.note: wearing something means having it around you, so it goes inside
cut short, the last letter drops

annotation.surface: Someone astonished they can get away with a very short garment.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a skimpy outfit; really MOR, cut short from MORE, wears HA plus I.
annotation.definitionFit: Mohair is a fabric made from the hair of the Angora goat.

entries.clue: Campaign very English in importance (8)

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

blocks.note: of great moment = of great importance

annotation.surface: A political campaign that is thoroughly English in character and significance.
annotation.walkthrough: Moment here is the old sense of weight or importance, not a point in time.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an organised effort for a cause, such as the suffragette movement, is a campaign.

entries.clue: Metallic element not often used as poison (6)

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

annotation.surface: A little-used metal that doubles as a poison.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a toxic metal such as arsenic; the element only gives its symbol.
annotation.definitionFit: Curare is a plant-derived poison used on South American arrow tips.

entries.clue: Shrewd Scots are not able to broadcast (5)

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard, so the word is judged by its sound

annotation.surface: Wily Scots refusing to go on air.
annotation.walkthrough: Canny is itself a Scots word, which makes the Scottish surface fit nicely.
annotation.definitionFit: Canny means shrewd, careful with judgment or money.

entries.clue: Nice friend finishes lace edging for mat (6)

indicators.note: the first piece finishes, comes at the end of, the second

blocks.note: tatting is handmade lace used for edging
ami is French for friend; Nice is the French city

annotation.surface: A friend in Nice putting the final lace trim on a table mat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nice' at the start of the clue hides its capital: it is the city in France, so the friend is French.
annotation.definitionFit: A tatami is a Japanese straw floor mat.

entries.clue: Recall parent, worrying in case I forget (8)

definitions.note: the definition is a sentence an amnesiac might say, standing for the person

indicators.note: calling back reverses the word
worried letters are fretted out of order

annotation.surface: Someone anxiously phoning their mother back in case they forget.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recall' and 'forget' make a memory theme; the definition is the confession 'I forget', which an amnesiac would say.
annotation.definitionFit: An amnesiac is someone who forgets, so 'I forget' describes one.

entries.clue: To speed over snow is the end of so many Russians (3)

definitions.text: the end of so many Russians

blocks.clueFragment: the end of so many Russians
blocks.note: the ending of countless Russian surnames

annotation.surface: A grim quip that skiing has killed many Russians.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pretends many Russians died skiing; 'end' means the end of their names, as in Dostoevski or Tchaikovski.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: the verb for gliding on runners over snow, and the ending of surnames like Tchaikovski.

entries.clue: Endlessly gnash teeth in unpleasant expression (4)

indicators.note: without its end, the last letter goes

blocks.note: to gnash teeth is to rub them together hard; 'Endlessly' takes off the final D

annotation.surface: Someone gnashing their teeth with a nasty look.
annotation.walkthrough: A grin is usually friendly, so 'unpleasant' seems wrong; an older sense is baring the teeth in pain or anger.
annotation.definitionFit: Grin can mean baring the teeth in a snarl or grimace.

entries.clue: Debtor absconding on the red-eye? (3-2-5)

definitions.note: the second definition is a description of the action, read as FLY BY NIGHT

blocks.note: a red-eye is an overnight flight

annotation.surface: A debtor dodging creditors by catching an overnight flight.
annotation.walkthrough: Red-eye is airline slang for a flight through the night, so taking one is literally to fly by night.
annotation.definitionFit: A fly-by-night is someone who flees at night to escape debts.
